The highest-weighted model of a fitted set

Source: R/pull_best.R
pull_best.Rd

Returns the candidate holding the most model weight in an object of class bayesmanecfit, as an object of class bayesnecfit. An object that is already a bayesnecfit is returned unchanged, so the caller does not have to test the class first.

pull_best(object, ...)

Arguments

object

An object of class bayesnecfit, bayesmanecfit or bayesnechurdlefit as returned by bnec.

...

Not used. Any argument supplied here is refused; see Details.

Value

For a bayesmanecfit, an object of class bayesnecfit. For a bayesnecfit, object unchanged. For a bayesnechurdlefit, an object of the same class with each component reduced to its own highest-weighted model.

Details

The highest-weighted candidate contributes most to the model-averaged estimate, so its fit is the one normally inspected with pp_check and check_fit. Selecting it by hand requires two things that are not obvious. The weights are held in mod_stats and pull_out takes a model name, so the name has to be found before it can be passed; and mod_stats exists on a bayesmanecfit alone, so the same code applied to a set that screen_models has reduced to one equation — which is returned as a bayesnecfit — reads a NULL. Both cases reach the same result here.

The weight selected on is reported along with the number of candidates it was selected from, since the two together are what says whether the selection means anything. The highest weight of a flat set of ten candidates is little more than the equal share of 0.1, and one such candidate describes the model-averaged estimate hardly at all. No warning is raised against a threshold, because what counts as a small weight depends on the size of the set, and a cut placed anywhere would be either noise on a set of two or false comfort on a set of twenty. summary reports the whole weights table, which is what a judgement of a marginal case needs.

Where two or more candidates hold exactly the same highest weight, the first in the order of the set is returned and the tie is reported. Only exact ties are detected; two weights differing in the last decimal place are not a tie and the larger is taken.

The object is the only argument. This function selects a model rather than re-specifying a fit, so x_range, resolution, sig_val and loo_controls are not accepted and are refused rather than ignored: honouring them on the bayesmanecfit branch, where pull_out rebuilds the fit, and ignoring them on the bayesnecfit branch, where nothing is rebuilt, would make the returned object depend on the class the caller was told not to test for. pull_out takes them alongside a model name, and amend rebuilds a fit that already exists.

Which equation was selected is reported on both branches, including the pass-through, so that a workflow leaves the same record whether or not the set had been reduced to one equation before the call. suppressMessages silences it.

The refusal of ... is raised in the generic, before dispatch, so a method written for another class outside this package cannot take an argument of its own either. screen_models and amend are closed to extension in the same way.

A bayesnechurdlefit is handled one component at a time and rewrapped, as screen_models and amend already do for that class. The two components may select different equations: the survival component is 0-1 bounded and the growth component need not be, so they do not hold the same candidates, let alone weight them alike.

See also

pull_out, screen_models, check_fit, summary

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(bayesnec)
data(manec_example)
best <- pull_best(manec_example)
check_fit(best)
# a bayesnecfit is returned unchanged, so this is safe on either class
pull_best(best)
} # }
